title: 1 Kings Chapter 3 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Kings chapter 3 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Kings Chapter 3 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Kings Chapter 3.

questions.question: Who did Solomon make an alliance with by marriage according to 1 Kings 3?
options: Pharaoh king of Egypt
King of Babylon
King of Assyria
King of Moab
questions.correctAnswer: Pharaoh king of Egypt
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 3:1 states that Solomon made an affinity with Pharaoh king of Egypt and took Pharaoh's daughter.

questions.question: Why did the people sacrifice in high places before Solomon’s reign?
options: Because there was no house built unto the name of the LORD
Because the king commanded it
Because the priests were there
Because of a famine in Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: Because there was no house built unto the name of the LORD
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 3:2 explains that the people sacrificed in high places because there was no house built unto the name of the LORD until those days.

questions.question: What did Solomon love and walk in according to 1 Kings 3?
options: The LORD and the statutes of David his father
The laws of Egypt
The traditions of the elders
The customs of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD and the statutes of David his father
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 3:3 states that Solomon loved the LORD and walked in the statutes of David his father.

questions.question: Where did Solomon go to offer a great number of burnt offerings?
options: Gibeon
Jerusalem
Bethel
Shiloh
questions.correctAnswer: Gibeon
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 3:4 tells us that Solomon went to Gibeon to sacrifice and offered a thousand burnt offerings upon that altar.

questions.question: How many burnt offerings did Solomon offer at Gibeon?
options: A thousand
Five hundred
Ten thousand
One hundred
questions.correctAnswer: A thousand
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 3:4 states that Solomon offered a thousand burnt offerings at Gibeon.

questions.question: What did the LORD say to Solomon in the dream at Gibeon?
options: Ask what I shall give thee
Build a house for Me
Gather your people
Go to Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: Ask what I shall give thee
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 3:5 records that the LORD appeared to Solomon in a dream and said, 'Ask what I shall give thee.'

questions.question: According to Solomon's prayer, how had God shown great mercy to David?
options: By giving him a son to sit on his throne
By granting him many riches
By giving him a long life
By defeating his enemies
questions.correctAnswer: By giving him a son to sit on his throne
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 3:6 states Solomon acknowledged God's mercy in giving David a son to sit on his throne as it was that day.

questions.question: How did Solomon describe himself when he asked for wisdom?
options: As a little child who knows not how to go out or come in
As a mighty warrior
As a learned scholar
As a wise man
questions.correctAnswer: As a little child who knows not how to go out or come in
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 3:7 records Solomon saying he is but a little child and knows not how to go out or come in.

questions.question: What did Solomon specifically ask God to give him?
options: An understanding heart to judge the people
Long life
Riches and honour
Victory over enemies
questions.correctAnswer: An understanding heart to judge the people
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 3:9 shows Solomon asked for an understanding heart to judge the people and discern between good and bad.

questions.question: How did the Lord react to Solomon's request for wisdom?
options: The speech pleased the Lord
The Lord was displeased
The Lord ignored the request
The Lord asked for more
questions.correctAnswer: The speech pleased the Lord
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 3:10 states that Solomon's speech pleased the Lord that he had asked for understanding.

questions.question: What did God promise Solomon because he asked not for riches or long life but for understanding?
options: A wise and understanding heart
An army of angels
A peaceful kingdom
A great temple
questions.correctAnswer: A wise and understanding heart
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 3:11-12 records God’s promise to give Solomon a wise and understanding heart because he asked for discernment.

questions.question: What additional blessings did God give Solomon besides wisdom?
options: Riches and honour
A long life
An eternal kingdom
Power over enemies
questions.correctAnswer: Riches and honour
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 3:13 states that God gave Solomon riches and honour in addition to wisdom.

questions.question: True or False: Solomon offered burnt offerings and peace offerings after waking from his dream.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 3:15 describes Solomon waking from the dream and offering burnt and peace offerings.

questions.question: True or False: Solomon sacrificed at the temple of the LORD in Jerusalem according to 1 Kings 3.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 3:4 says Solomon went to Gibeon to sacrifice, which was the great high place, not the temple in Jerusalem.

questions.question: True or False: The people sacrificed in high places because Solomon commanded it.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 3:2 explains that people sacrificed in high places because no house of the LORD was built, not because Solomon commanded it.

medium.title: 1 Kings Chapter 3 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Kings Chapter 3 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What reason did God give Solomon for granting him a wise and understanding heart?
options: Because Solomon asked for long life and riches
Because Solomon asked for understanding to discern judgment and did not ask for riches or the life of his enemies
Because Solomon asked for the defeat of his enemies
Because Solomon asked for a large kingdom
questions.correctAnswer: Because Solomon asked for understanding to discern judgment and did not ask for riches or the life of his enemies
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 3:11 states that God granted Solomon wisdom because he asked for understanding to judge rather than long life, riches, or harm to enemies.

questions.question: How is Solomon's wisdom described in relation to others before and after him?
options: He was as wise as many kings before him
No one was like him before or after in wisdom and understanding
His wisdom was common among kings
He was wise only compared to his father David
questions.correctAnswer: No one was like him before or after in wisdom and understanding
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 3:12 explains that God gave Solomon a wise and understanding heart unlike any other before or after him.

questions.question: According to 1 Kings 3, what additional blessings did God give Solomon beyond what he asked for?
options: Only wisdom and understanding
Riches and honor along with wisdom
Long life and many children
Victory over enemies
questions.correctAnswer: Riches and honor along with wisdom
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 3:13 states God gave Solomon riches and honor in addition to the understanding he asked for.

questions.question: What condition did God attach to the promise of lengthening Solomon's days?
options: If Solomon built many houses
If Solomon walked in God's ways and kept His statutes and commandments
If Solomon defeated his enemies
If Solomon sacrificed many burnt offerings
questions.correctAnswer: If Solomon walked in God's ways and kept His statutes and commandments
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 3:14 shows God promised longer life if Solomon obeyed His laws as David did.

questions.question: What did Solomon do immediately after waking from the dream in which God appeared to him?
options: He built a temple
He offered burnt offerings and peace offerings and made a feast for his servants
He went to war
He wrote a book
questions.correctAnswer: He offered burnt offerings and peace offerings and made a feast for his servants
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 3:15 records that after awakening, Solomon went to the ark, offered sacrifices, and feasted with his servants.

questions.question: What was the relationship of the two women who came before Solomon in 1 Kings 3?
options: They were sisters
They were strangers from different towns
They were harlots dwelling in the same house
They were relatives of Solomon
questions.correctAnswer: They were harlots dwelling in the same house
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 3:16 and 3:17 describe the two women as harlots living together in one house.

questions.question: According to the first woman’s account, what happened to her child?
options: The child was taken by strangers
The child died because she overlaid it during the night
The child ran away
The child was healthy and alive
questions.correctAnswer: The child died because she overlaid it during the night
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 3:19 tells that the first woman's child died at night because she overlaid it.

questions.question: How did the first woman describe the exchange of the babies during the night?
options: She gave her child away willingly
The other woman took her son while she slept and laid her dead child in her bosom
Both women exchanged children by agreement
The children were born at different times
questions.correctAnswer: The other woman took her son while she slept and laid her dead child in her bosom
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 3:20 describes the other woman taking the living son from the first woman’s side while she slept and placing her dead child there.

questions.question: What was the dispute between the two women when they came before Solomon?
options: Which woman had more children
Which woman was the mother of the living child
Who should pay more taxes
Who should be punished for stealing
questions.correctAnswer: Which woman was the mother of the living child
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 3:22 shows the women argued over whose child was alive and whose was dead.

questions.question: What proposal did Solomon make to resolve the dispute between the two women?
options: To give the child to the first woman
To divide the living child in two and give half to each woman
To send the child away to be raised elsewhere
To let the priests decide
questions.correctAnswer: To divide the living child in two and give half to each woman
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 3:25 records Solomon’s proposal to cut the living child in two to settle the claim.

questions.question: How did the woman who was the true mother react to Solomon’s proposal to divide the child?
options: She agreed to the division
She asked the king to give the child to the other woman so it would not be killed
She fled the court
She asked for time to think
questions.correctAnswer: She asked the king to give the child to the other woman so it would not be killed
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 3:26 shows the true mother pleaded to spare the child and give it to the other woman rather than dividing it.

questions.question: What conclusion did Solomon make based on the reactions of the two women to his proposal?
options: That the child belonged to neither woman
That the woman who pleaded for the child's life was the true mother
That both women were lying
That the child should be given to the king
questions.correctAnswer: That the woman who pleaded for the child's life was the true mother
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 3:27 explains Solomon declared the woman who wanted to spare the child was the real mother.

questions.question: What was the public reaction in Israel to Solomon’s wise judgment?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 3:28 states that all Israel heard of Solomon’s judgment and feared him, recognizing the wisdom of God in him.

questions.question: Does 1 Kings 3 promise that Solomon’s days will be lengthened only if he builds many houses?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 3:14 promises lengthened days if Solomon walks in God's ways and keeps His commandments, not based on building houses.

questions.question: How does 1 Kings 3 teach about the importance of humility in leadership?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Solomon acknowledges his youth and inexperience in 1 Kings 3:7 and asks God for an understanding heart to judge, demonstrating humility in leadership.

hard.title: 1 Kings Chapter 3 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Kings Chapter 3.

questions.question: What was the reason Solomon gave for asking God for an understanding heart?
options: He was a young king who did not know how to govern
He wanted riches and honor
He desired a long life
He wished to defeat his enemies
questions.correctAnswer: He was a young king who did not know how to govern
questions.explanation: Solomon stated he was but a little child and did not know how to go out or come in, showing his need for wisdom to govern (1 Kings 3:7-9).

questions.question: What was God's response to Solomon's request for wisdom?
options: God refused to grant wisdom
God granted wisdom along with riches and honor
God only granted riches
God granted a long life instead
questions.correctAnswer: God granted wisdom along with riches and honor
questions.explanation: God granted Solomon a wise and understanding heart and also gave him riches and honor, which he had not asked for (1 Kings 3:11-13).

questions.question: Where did Solomon go to offer a thousand burnt offerings?
options: Jerusalem
Gibeon
Mount Sinai
Bethel
questions.correctAnswer: Gibeon
questions.explanation: Solomon went to Gibeon, the great high place, to offer a thousand burnt offerings (1 Kings 3:4).

questions.question: What action did Solomon take after awakening from the dream in which God spoke to him?
options: He built a new altar
He offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before the ark
He immediately began building the temple
He sent envoys to Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: He offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before the ark
questions.explanation: After waking, Solomon came to Jerusalem and stood before the ark of the covenant, offering burnt and peace offerings (1 Kings 3:15).

questions.question: What was the dispute between the two women who came before Solomon?
options: They argued over payment for services
They disputed ownership of a living child
They disagreed about building materials
They contended over land boundaries
questions.correctAnswer: They disputed ownership of a living child
questions.explanation: Two women, both claiming to be the mother of the living child, disputed before Solomon (1 Kings 3:16-22).

questions.question: How did Solomon propose to resolve the dispute between the two women?
options: He asked for witnesses
He ordered the child to be divided in two
He gave the child to the woman who could pay
He deferred the case to the priests
questions.correctAnswer: He ordered the child to be divided in two
questions.explanation: Solomon said, 'Divide the living child in two, and give half to the one, and half to the other' (1 Kings 3:25).

questions.question: What was the reaction of the woman who truly loved the living child to Solomon's proposal?
options: She agreed to divide the child
She asked that the child be given to the other woman
She pleaded to save the child's life by giving it to the other woman
She ran away
questions.correctAnswer: She pleaded to save the child's life by giving it to the other woman
questions.explanation: The true mother pleaded, 'O my lord, give her the living child, and in no wise slay it' (1 Kings 3:26).

questions.question: What conclusion did Solomon reach about the true mother based on her reaction?
options: She was the one who wanted to divide the child
She was the mother who wished to save the child's life
She was lying about the child
She was indifferent to the child's fate
questions.correctAnswer: She was the mother who wished to save the child's life
questions.explanation: Solomon concluded that the woman who showed compassion and pleaded for the child's life was the true mother (1 Kings 3:27).

questions.question: What was the public reaction in Israel to Solomon's judgment in the case of the two women?
options: They were angered and rebelled
They ignored the judgment
They feared the king and recognized the wisdom of God in him
They doubted Solomon's wisdom
questions.correctAnswer: They feared the king and recognized the wisdom of God in him
questions.explanation: All Israel heard of Solomon's judgment and feared the king because they saw the wisdom of God in him (1 Kings 3:28).

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of divine wisdom granted to a king as seen in 1 Kings 3?
options: James 1:5
Genesis 1:1
Revelation 21:1
Psalm 23:1
questions.correctAnswer: James 1:5
questions.explanation: James 1:5 encourages believers to ask God for wisdom who gives liberally, echoing the theme of God granting wisdom as to Solomon in 1 Kings 3:5.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word translated as 'understanding heart' (1 Kings 3:9) most closely mean?
options: Compassionate soul
Discerning mind and insight
Physical strength
Emotional passion
questions.correctAnswer: Discerning mind and insight
questions.explanation: The Hebrew term 'leb bin' (heart of understanding) refers to discernment and insight, crucial for judging rightly as Solomon requested (1 Kings 3:9).

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in the narrative of Solomon’s judgment involving the two women?
options: Chiasmus
Parable
Allegory
Foreshadowing
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasmus
questions.explanation: The story is structured chiastically, with the dispute and Solomon’s proposal mirroring each other to highlight the wisdom in his judgment (1 Kings 3:16-27).

questions.question: True or False: Solomon asked God for long life and riches instead of wisdom.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Solomon did not ask for long life or riches but for an understanding heart to judge the people (1 Kings 3:11).

questions.question: True or False: Solomon’s judgment involving the two women led to all Israel fearing the king because they recognized God’s wisdom in him.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The text states that all Israel feared Solomon after hearing his judgment and recognized the wisdom of God in him (1 Kings 3:28).

questions.question: What role did the ark of the covenant play after Solomon’s dream and before the judgment of the two women?
options: It was the location where Solomon received the dream
Solomon stood before it to offer sacrifices after awakening
It was moved to Gibeon for the sacrifices
It was hidden from the people
questions.correctAnswer: Solomon stood before it to offer sacrifices after awakening
questions.explanation: After his dream, Solomon stood before the ark of the covenant in Jerusalem and offered burnt and peace offerings (1 Kings 3:15).

theological.title: 1 Kings Chapter 3 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Kings Chapter 3 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What theological significance does Solomon's request for an understanding heart to judge the people reveal about divine wisdom?
options: It shows Solomon valued political power over spiritual insight
It reveals a desire to govern justly by God's guidance
It implies Solomon wanted to avoid responsibility
It indicates Solomon sought personal wealth and honor
questions.correctAnswer: It reveals a desire to govern justly by God's guidance
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 3:9 shows Solomon asking God for an understanding heart to discern judgment so he can govern God's chosen people rightly, emphasizing the theological importance of divine wisdom for just leadership.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is primarily demonstrated by God granting Solomon wisdom and understanding, surpassing all others before and after him?
options: Omnipresence
Omniscience
Sovereignty
Immutability
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 3:12 emphasizes God's sovereign authority to bestow unparalleled wisdom and understanding upon Solomon, illustrating God's control over granting gifts and status.

questions.question: How does Solomon's dream encounter with God at Gibeon (1 Kings 3:5) typologically foreshadow Christ's role as the ultimate wise King?
options: Both kings receive direct divine revelation
Both establish political alliances through marriage
Both offer burnt offerings on high places
Both are rejected by their people
questions.correctAnswer: Both kings receive direct divine revelation
questions.explanation: In 1 Kings 3:5, God appears to Solomon in a dream granting wisdom, foreshadowing Christ who embodies divine wisdom and receives direct revelation as the ultimate King (cf. Colossians 2:3).

questions.question: What doctrine is illustrated by Solomon’s humility in acknowledging his youth and inexperience before God in his prayer (1 Kings 3:7)?
options: The sinfulness of man
The priesthood of all believers
The necessity of divine grace
The sovereignty of human will
questions.correctAnswer: The necessity of divine grace
questions.explanation: Solomon’s admission in 1 Kings 3:7 that he is 'but a little child' who does not know how to govern illustrates human dependence on God’s grace for guidance and wisdom, a key doctrine of sanctification and divine enablement.

questions.question: According to 1 Kings 3:14, what conditional promise does God make to Solomon concerning his life span?
options: God promises Solomon eternal life unconditionally
God promises to lengthen Solomon's days if he walks in God's statutes
God promises Solomon wealth if he conquers enemies
God promises Solomon fame regardless of his actions
questions.correctAnswer: God promises to lengthen Solomon's days if he walks in God's statutes
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 3:14 states God will lengthen Solomon’s days conditional on Solomon’s obedience to God’s commandments, emphasizing the covenantal principle of blessing contingent on faithfulness.

questions.question: What narrative arc connection does Solomon’s building of the house of the LORD (1 Kings 3:1) have with the broader redemptive story of Scripture?
options: It signifies the establishment of the monarchy over Israel
It prefigures the coming of Christ as the true temple
It symbolizes Israel's rejection of God
It marks the end of prophetic activity
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures the coming of Christ as the true temple
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 3:1 situates Solomon's building of the LORD's house within the redemptive narrative, prefiguring Christ as the ultimate temple where God dwells among His people (John 2:19-21).

questions.question: How does the story of the two women and the living child (1 Kings 3:16-28) demonstrate the practical application of divine wisdom in judgment?
options: By showing Solomon’s ability to detect lies through evidence
By illustrating the role of sacrifice in legal disputes
By revealing God's wisdom in resolving complex human conflicts
By emphasizing strict legalism without mercy
questions.correctAnswer: By revealing God's wisdom in resolving complex human conflicts
questions.explanation: The judgment in 1 Kings 3:16-28 reveals how Solomon applies God-given wisdom to discern truth and administer justice, demonstrating divine wisdom's role in governance and human affairs.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight is conveyed by Solomon’s prayer (1 Kings 3:6-9) and God’s response (1 Kings 3:11-13)?
options: The doctrine of divine election and human free will
The doctrine of sanctification and perseverance
The doctrine of wisdom as a divine gift and its blessings
The doctrine of predestination and reprobation
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of wisdom as a divine gift and its blessings
questions.explanation: Together, 1 Kings 3:6-9 and 11-13 teach that wisdom is a gracious divine gift granted according to God's sovereign will, accompanied by blessings like riches and honor, underscoring God's generosity in bestowing what is truly good.

questions.question: What does 1 Kings 3:2 reveal about Israel’s worship practices before the temple was built, and what theological issue does this raise?
options: They worshipped idols exclusively, raising the issue of idolatry
They sacrificed in high places, raising issues about centralized worship
They had no form of worship, raising the issue of spiritual neglect
They worshipped only in Solomon’s palace, raising issues of royal control
questions.correctAnswer: They sacrificed in high places, raising issues about centralized worship
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 3:2 notes sacrifices were made in high places due to the absence of a temple, highlighting the tension between proper centralized worship in the LORD’s house and decentralized practices that later prophets critique (Deuteronomy 12:5-14).

questions.question: How does Solomon's alliance with Pharaoh and taking of Pharaoh's daughter (1 Kings 3:1) reflect the theological tension between faithfulness to God and political expediency?
options: It shows complete faithfulness without compromise
It illustrates a compromise that risks idolatry
It indicates rejection of God’s covenant
It signifies the end of Israel’s monarchy
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates a compromise that risks idolatry
questions.explanation: In 1 Kings 3:1, Solomon’s political alliance through marriage to Pharaoh's daughter introduces tension between faithfulness to God’s covenant and worldly alliances that later biblical texts associate with idolatry risks (cf. 1 Kings 11:1-4).

questions.question: What theological truth about God's justice and wisdom is revealed in Solomon’s judgment involving the living child and the proposed division (1 Kings 3:25-27)?
options: God’s wisdom is limited to religious matters
True wisdom discerns the heart beyond mere words
Justice requires harsh punishment
God is indifferent to human suffering
questions.correctAnswer: True wisdom discerns the heart beyond mere words
questions.explanation: Solomon’s proposal to divide the child in 1 Kings 3:25-27 exposes the true mother’s heart, showing that divine wisdom penetrates beyond surface claims to the realities of human intentions and emotions.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that divine wisdom in the Old Testament is merely human cleverness. What does 1 Kings 3:10-13 actually teach about the origin and nature of Solomon's wisdom?
options: Solomon’s wisdom was entirely his own natural ability
Solomon’s wisdom was a divine gift granted by God’s sovereign will
Solomon’s wisdom was acquired through Egyptian education
Solomon’s wisdom was limited and did not impress Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Solomon’s wisdom was a divine gift granted by God’s sovereign will
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 3:10-13 clearly states that Solomon’s wisdom pleased the Lord, who granted it according to Solomon’s request, underscoring wisdom as a gracious divine endowment, not mere human cleverness (James 1:5).

questions.question: What combined theological insight about the relationship between divine blessing and human obedience is found by comparing 1 Kings 3:14 and 1 Kings 3:13?
options: Blessings are automatic regardless of conduct
Blessings are guaranteed only through military conquest
Blessings like long life, riches, and honor are linked to walking in God's ways
Blessings are unrelated to obedience but to royal lineage
questions.correctAnswer: Blessings like long life, riches, and honor are linked to walking in God's ways
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 3:13 promises riches and honor, and 3:14 conditions long life on obedience, teaching that divine blessings are connected to covenant faithfulness and walking in God's statutes.

questions.question: How does Solomon's act of offering a thousand burnt offerings at Gibeon (1 Kings 3:4) illustrate the worship theology of Israel prior to the temple’s completion?
options: It shows a rejection of sacrificial worship
It reflects the centrality of high places in worship before the temple
It indicates that worship was only done by priests
It demonstrates that sacrifices were only symbolic, not real
questions.correctAnswer: It reflects the centrality of high places in worship before the temple
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 3:4 records Solomon's large-scale sacrifices at the high place in Gibeon, illustrating how Israel worshiped at such sites before the temple was built, showing transitional worship practices.

questions.question: What doctrinal principle concerning God's kindness and covenant faithfulness is taught through Solomon's acknowledgment of God's mercy to David (1 Kings 3:6)?
options: God's kindness is conditional on human perfection
God's mercy extends across generations in covenant faithfulness
God forgets former promises with new kings
God's covenant is only for the present king
questions.correctAnswer: God's mercy extends across generations in covenant faithfulness
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 3:6 shows Solomon recognizing God's great mercy to David and the fulfillment of covenant promises through Solomon’s kingship, teaching that God's kindness is steadfast and generational.
